title: SAFELOC: Overcoming Data Poisoning Attacks in Heterogeneous Federated Machine Learning for Indoor Localization
problem: Indoor localization systems suffer from device heterogeneity (hardware/software variations across mobile devices) and ML data poisoning attacks, compromising both accuracy and model efficiency for deployment.
motivation: Mobile indoor localization requires robustness to heterogeneous devices and adversarial data poisoning while maintaining compact models for resource-constrained deployment.
method: SAFELOC combines a fused neural network performing concurrent poisoning detection and localization with federated learning, employing a dynamic saliency map-based aggregation strategy that adapts based on detected poisoning severity.
key_novelty: Dynamic saliency-map-driven federated aggregation that adapts poisoning defense to attack severity while maintaining model compactness.
contributions: Fused neural network architecture combining poisoning detection and localization in single model
5.9× improvement in mean localization error over SOTA
2.1× reduction in inference latency with compact model footprint
primary_theme: federated learning for robust heterogeneous mobile localization
